overview.description: Amerikaner is a highly popular Norwegian trick-taking game that combines elements of bidding, secret partnerships, and a kitty exchange. Despite its name, the game is uniquely Scandinavian and features a distinct 'trump-on-the-lead' mechanic where the bidder's first card determines the trump suit and their partner simultaneously.

history.origins: Originating in Norway, the game's name 'Amerikaner' is a mystery to historians, as it bears little resemblance to standard American card games. It belongs to the broader 'Boston' family of bidding games that were fashionable in Northern Europe in the late 19th century.
timeline: Early 20th C.: Emerges as a staple social game in Norway.
1950s-70s: Becomes a popular variant in Scandinavian student clubs.
Present: Widely played in Norway, often in casual social settings.
history.evolution: The game evolved to include a 'Kitty' (Talon) phase, which allows the bidder to significantly strengthen their hand before play.
history.cultural: In Norway, 'Amerikaner' refers specifically to this game, whereas in other countries it might be confused with 'American' versions of Whist or Bridge.

setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 12 cards, one at a time. The remaining 4 cards are placed face down in the center to form the 'Kitty'.

rules.objective: High bidder must win at least the number of tricks they bid (with their secret partner), or all 12 tricks (if bidding Amerikaner).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding**: Staring left of the dealer, players bid a number of tricks from 6 to 12. Each bid must be higher than the last. 2. **Amerikaner Bid**: The highest possible bid, an commitment to win all 12 tricks without a partner. 3. **The Kitty**: The high bidder takes the 4 kitty cards and discards any 4 cards face down. 4. **Calling the Partner**: The bidder leads the first card. The suit of this card becomes trumps. As they lead, they name a specific card of that suit (e.g., 'The Ace of Spades'). The player holding that card is the secret partner. 5. **Play**: Standard trick-taking rules. Highest card of led suit or highest trump wins the trick.
keyRules: Trump Suit: Always the suit of the very first lead made by the bidder.
Grand: An optional bid in some variations where there is no trump suit.
Secret Partner: Must play the called card to the first trick if possible.
Amerikaner Win: If the bidder takes all 12 tricks alone, it is a massive score (+52).

strategy.basic: If you have a strong suit but lack the top card (the Ace), bid high (8 or 9) and call the Ace of that suit to guarantee a powerful partner.
strategy.intermediate: The Discard: When using the kitty, discard cards from a suit you are 'short' in. This allows you to trump into that suit early in the game.
strategy.advanced: Defensive play for opponents: If you suspect a partner has been called, try to 'bleed' the bidder's trumps early to prevent them from cross-ruffing.
tips: Don't bid 12 unless you have a near-perfect hand. If you lose even one trick, you lose 12 points while your opponents gain from their captured tricks.
Remember: the bidder MUST lead the trump suit first.

list.name: No-Kitty Variant
list.description: All 52 cards are dealt (13 each). The minimum bid is increased to 7.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant is documented but engine-level parameter changes are not yet modeled.

list.name: Joker Variant
list.description: Jokers are added. A led Joker wins the trick automatically. If discarded when void, it has no power.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Joker rules are described in sources but specific engine overrides still need to be derived.

difficulty.easy: Bids 6 randomly. Fails to discard effectively from the kitty. Doesn't recognize who their partner is until revealed.
difficulty.medium: Bids based on suit length. Calls the Ace of their longest suit to find a partner.
difficulty.hard: Calculates the probability of cards in the kitty based on the bidding patterns. Strategically discards to create a 'Long Trump' scenario. As an opponent, counts tricks to ensure the bidder falls one short.

considerations: AI must factor in the 'Secret Partner' mechanicâ€”they may be playing against their own partner for the first trick.
The 'Kitty' exchange is a major optimization point for the AI.

ante.reason: Amerikaner uses trick bids and kitty; no ante.

deal.reason: Deal via customActions deal_cards and create_kitty.

reveal_market.reason: No market; trump set by bidder's first lead.

buy_market.reason: No market; high bidder takes kitty via take_kitty.

buy_stock.reason: No stock purchase; kitty is taken once by bidder.

fold.reason: Partnership trick-taking; all play every trick.

check.reason: No betting; scoring by tricks and bid outcome.

call.reason: No betting; partner called by card name on lead.

bet.reason: Amerikaner scores by tricks and bid, not chips.

draw.reason: No draw pile; bidder takes kitty once via take_kitty.

discard.reason: Kitty discard via custom discard_four after take_kitty.

pass.description: Pass without taking another action this turn.
pass.constraints: Allowed when rules permit skipping a wager or play.

go_out.reason: Hand ends when all 12 tricks are played.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for this German-style trick-taking and scoring game.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Trump and plain-suit order apply as in the game rules; follow suit when possible. Suit may determine scoring and trick value in Amerikaner.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit in the order used by the game (ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two). Trick and scoring order follow the variant rules.

hero.title: AMERIKANER
hero.subtitle: The Norwegian Mystery
hero.tagline: Bid your tricks, call your partner, and keep the secret until the first trick.

synthesis.shortDescription: Norway's favorite bidding game. A tactical battle of secret partnerships where the bidder chooses the trump and their ally with a single lead.

prompts.human: Welcome to Amerikaner. You have 12 cards. There's a 4-card kitty in the middle. Bid how many tricks you think you can take with a partner. If you win the bid, your first lead will set the trumps and name your secret partner. Be careful with those 52-point Amerikaner bids!
prompts.ai: Game: Amerikaner. Type: Secret Partnership Trick-taking. Players: 4. Rules: 12 cards each, 4 card kitty. Bid 6-12. Amerikaner = 12 solo. Lead sets trump and names partner card. Goal: Reach 100 points.

scoring.description: Points are awarded based on whether the bid was successful.
scoring.winCondition: The bidder and partner score the bid amount if successful. Opponents score 1 point for every trick they capture.

penalties.Bid Failed: The bidder and partner BOTH subtract the bid amount from their scores.
penalties.Amerikaner Failure: A failed Amerikaner bid results in a -52 penalty.

scoring.splitRules: If the bid succeeds, early 'Amerikaner' rules state the bidder and partner share the credit equally.

nullReasons.cardValues: Amerikaner scores by tricks and bid outcome; there are no per-card point values.
